_comment: Rules of the Player's Handbook (2024): the Rules Glossary, the rules sections of chapters 1, 2, 6 and 7 and Appendix A; and the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024): the sections of its chapters, the DM's Toolbox systems and the parts left out (EXPANSIONS.md section 1.3). Names, pages and classification only.

entries.name: Adventure
entries.note: omitted: a word for the DM's story; quests, sites and dungeons serve it (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3, DM advice as design guidance)

entries.name: Alignment
entries.note: omitted: alignment stays a field of stat blocks and sentient items only; no player alignment (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Attitude
entries.note: adapted: no DM; a band's attitude comes from its leader's alignment and mood, and a fight turns it hostile or indifferent

entries.name: Campaign
entries.note: omitted: a word for the DM's long story; the living world and its history play this part (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3, DM advice)

entries.name: Carrying Capacity
entries.note: adapted: 15 pounds per Strength point, then encumbered and heavily encumbered tiers; pushing, dragging and lifting are not counted

entries.name: Challenge Rating
entries.note: adapted: stat blocks carry CR and XP; encounters are built from XP budgets by the game, not by a DM

entries.name: Curses
entries.note: adapted: curses on magic items (hidden until identified, bind the wearer); curses on creatures wait for the Crypts and Curses expansion

entries.name: Dead
entries.note: adapted: in a fight dying is by the book; outside one 0 hit points is down, not dead, and the world records the death

entries.name: Dehydration [Hazard]
entries.note: adapted: thirst is a meter in the body system that ends in exhaustion, instead of the book's one-level-a-day rule

entries.name: Encounter
entries.note: adapted: combat encounters are built from XP budgets by the game on the road and in places; social ones run as conversations and parley

entries.name: Friendly [Attitude]
entries.note: adapted: Influence checks against a fixed DC replace the DM's ruling on a friendly creature's help

entries.name: Healing
entries.note: adapted: hit points come back as in the book, but wounds, blood loss and infection still need tending on top (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: High Jump
entries.note: adapted: only the long jump is used on the battle mat; a high jump would only reach a flier, and the mat counts a flier's height in reach already

entries.name: Hit Points
entries.note: adapted: the game's own wounds, blood and pain sit on top of hit points; the 0 hit point and death save rules are the book's.

entries.name: Improvised Weapons
entries.note: adapted: a bow or crossbow swung at close quarters; held tools and torches are not weapons, and throwing a blade without the Thrown property is left out (the Auto would throw away its only weapon)

entries.name: Influence [Action]
entries.note: adapted: no DM, so the DC comes from data and the foe's attitude; talk is a battle action or a conversation choice.

entries.name: Knocking Out a Creature
entries.note: adapted: the game asks when a party member's melee blow would kill a humanoid; the one knocked out is taken alive, a prisoner after the fight

entries.name: Long Rest
entries.note: adapted: restores hit points, Hit Point Dice and features as the book says, but wounds still need tending and the body still needs food and warmth.

entries.name: Malnutrition [Hazard]
entries.note: adapted: hunger and thirst are the game's own survival meters; strain from them builds exhaustion, 2 off d20 tests per level.

entries.name: Short Rest
entries.note: adapted: Hit Point Dice are spent on rest automatically; wounds and the body's needs still run on top.

entries.name: Simultaneous Effects
entries.note: adapted: the engine resolves effects in turn and event order; the player is not asked to pick an order.

entries.name: Telepathy
entries.note: adapted: kept on every stat block with its range; no creature of this expansion has it, and Influence in a fight does not yet ask for a shared language (it will when languages matter)

entries.name: Player or DM?
entries.note: omitted: the game itself is the Dungeon Master; there is no human DM role (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Rhythm of Play
entries.note: omitted: DM advice, used as design guidance (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: An Ongoing Game
entries.note: omitted: campaign advice; the world, its history and the save keep the game going (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Social Interaction
entries.note: adapted: Influence is a chosen conversation option or battle parley; attitudes (Friendly, Indifferent, Hostile) are data and shift advantage

entries.name: Hazards
entries.note: adapted: falling, fire and suffocation follow the book; cold, thirst, hunger and disease use the game's own survival systems on top

entries.name: Movement and Position
entries.note: adapted: a grid of 5-foot squares with heights and leaps; difficult terrain, crawling and climbing cost extra feet as in the book

entries.name: Hit Points
entries.note: adapted: hit points sit under the game's blood, wounds and pain systems; outside battle 0 is down, not dead (Fair chances)

entries.name: Healing
entries.note: adapted: healing also stops bleeding and treats wounds by the game's health systems; rests take real time and supplies

entries.name: Dropping to 0 Hit Points
entries.note: adapted: death saves in battle as the book says; outside battle 0 hit points leaves you senseless, not dead

entries.name: Step 4: Choose an Alignment
entries.note: Section 1.3: alignment stays a field of stat blocks and sentient items; there is no alignment system for the player.

entries.name: Tiers of Play
entries.note: adapted: the tiers set how far the worst lands' bands grow and how much a named beast of the history has grown

entries.name: Coins
entries.note: adapted: coins weigh 50 to the pound and a purse holds the fewest coins; the game counts in gold, silver and copper

entries.name: Tools
entries.note: The rules of the section (proficiency adds the bonus, with the skill as well advantage); the tools themselves are in equipment.json.

entries.name: One Spell with a Spell Slot per Turn
Chapter 1: The Basics
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content.

entries.name: Chapter 2: Running the Game (DM advice)
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content. Covers: Know Your Players, Group Size, Multiple DMs, Narration, Improvising Answers, Roleplaying, Using a Map, Tracking Initiative, Tracking Monsters' Hit Points, Using and Tracking Conditions, Tracking Position at Long Range, Narration in Combat, Keeping Combat Moving, Adjusting Difficulty.

entries.name: Resolving Outcomes
entries.note: omitted: DM advice, used as design guidance (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Ability Checks
entries.note: adapted: the game picks the DC from fixed numbers in data (study, locks, travel pace) instead of a DM's judgement

entries.name: Attack Rolls
entries.note: omitted: DM advice, used as design guidance (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries.note: adapted: DCs come from stat blocks, spells and data, not the DM's pick

entries.name: Difficulty Class
entries.note: adapted: DCs are fixed numbers in data (easy 10 to very hard 25), not set by a DM

entries.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
entries.note: adapted: the game decides by fixed reasons (attitude, conditions, cover) instead of DM discretion

entries.name: Consequences
entries.note: omitted: DM advice, used as design guidance (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Improvising Damage
entries.note: adapted: traps, falls and fire use fixed damage tables in data instead of improvised numbers

entries.name: Running Social Interaction
entries.note: adapted: conversations are written choices with whitelisted outcomes; attitude and standing replace DM roleplay

entries.name: Attitude
entries.note: advantage with the Friendly, disadvantage with the Hostile, as written; the Influence DC (15 or their best Intelligence) is eased by 3 and then moved by numbers, being seen first and hurts, so that talking past an even band is as hard as before Part D (Fair Chances)

entries.name: Running Exploration
entries.note: adapted: the game runs travel, light, searching and time itself, with no DM to rule

entries.name: Actions in Exploration
entries.note: adapted: exploration actions are menu commands (search, unlock, forage, rest) with fixed DCs

entries.name: Underwater Encounter Distance
entries.note: With underwater combat (Expansion 22), by theme.

entries.name: Weather
entries.note: With the environmental effects (Expansion 13), by theme; the game's own weather stays.

entries.name: Travel Terrain
entries.note: the maximum pace by land; encounter distance and foraging DCs are the game's own

entries.name: Miniatures
entries.note: omitted: tabletop miniatures advice; the battle mat is the game's own grid (EXPANSIONS.md 1.3)

entries.name: Awarding Heroic Inspiration
entries.note: omitted: DM advice on awarding it; the game gives it by the Resourceful trait each long rest and spends it in Battle._save

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries.note: adapted: experience points and discovery XP in data, with levels to 10 for now; no DM milestone choice

entries.name: Variant: Training to Gain Levels
entries.note: omitted: a level comes at once, as it always has (CLAUDE.md); a wait to train would only stand between the player and the rules they have earned

entries.name: Alignment
entries.note: Section 1.3: alignment stays a field of stat blocks and sentient items (and matters on the planes, Expansion 26); there is no alignment system for the player.

entries.name: Starting Attitude
entries.note: by the leader's alignment, weighted towards Hostile for bands met as trouble

entries.name: Creating a Background
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's tools for the DM's own creations are used as guidance whenever Realmwalker invents something of its own.

entries.name: Creating a Creature
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's tools for the DM's own creations are used as guidance whenever Realmwalker invents something of its own.

entries.name: Creating a Magic Item
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's tools for the DM's own creations are used as guidance whenever Realmwalker invents something of its own.

entries.name: Creating a Spell
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's tools for the DM's own creations are used as guidance whenever Realmwalker invents something of its own.

entries.name: Demonic Possession
entries.note: Printed as an environmental curse in Curses and Magical Contagions.

entries.name: Environmental Effects
entries.note: Its planar effects are in world.json (Expansion 26).

entries.name: Firearms and Explosives
entries.note: Renaissance items only, as rare gnomish inventions; the modern and futuristic ones are left out (section 1.3).

entries.name: Alien Technology
entries.note: Section 1.3: the DMG's modern and futuristic weapons and its alien technology break the setting.

entries.name: Gods and Other Powers
entries.note: The named gods of the multiverse are not transplanted; each world has its own faiths (section 1.3).

entries.name: Adjudicating Areas of Effect
entries.note: Printed in Mobs: how many targets an area catches without a grid.

entries.name: Nonplayer Characters
entries.note: Nonplayer characters and attitudes in depth (Appendix E).

entries.name: Settlements
entries.note: Its traits and calamities are in world.json.

entries.name: Supernatural Gifts
entries.note: Its blessings and charms are in world.json.

entries.name: Chapter 4: Creating Adventures (DM advice)
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content. Covers: Step-by-Step Adventures, Lay Out the Premise, Adventure Premise, Adventure Conflict, Adventure Situations by Level, Adventure Setting, Draw In the Players, Adventure Patrons, Supernatural Hooks, Happenstance Hooks, Plan Encounters, Character Objectives, Keeping the Adventure Moving, Something for Everyone, Multiple Ways to Progress, Social Interaction Encounters, Exploration Encounters, Encounter Pace and Tension, Bring It to an End, Denouement, Adventure Examples.

entries.name: Combat Encounters
entries.note: bands are built for the land's danger (a party level), not the party; the budget trims a band, never past the last of a kind, and a lone traveller still meets fewer of the rank and file (Fair Chances)

entries.name: Random Encounters
entries.note: the game's own encounter tables by land, danger and hour, sized by the XP budget

entries.name: Treasure Hoards
entries.note: CR 11-16 money: the book prints 8d8 x 10,000 with an average of 36,000; the average is kept (x 1,000)

entries.name: Quest Rewards
entries.note: the giver pays the coin the terms say (a village cannot pay a hoard); for great works a lord, priest or headman adds the hoard row's magic items

entries.name: Chapter 5: Creating Campaigns
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content.

entries.name: Greyhawk
entries.note: Section 1.3: Greyhawk is not transplanted; Realmwalker's worlds are generated and have their own faiths.

entries.name: Other Configurations
entries.note: Expansion 26 chooses how Realmwalker's planes are arranged.

entries.name: Alignment and the Outer Planes
entries.note: Alignment matters on the planes (section 1.3); Planar Dissonance is in world.json.

entries.name: Spells
entries.note: The spells that reach other planes, under Planar Travel.

entries.name: Traveling the Outer Planes
entries.note: Its four crossings are in world.json.

entries.name: Planar Adventure Situations
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content.

entries.name: Tour of the Multiverse
entries.note: Each plane has its own entry in world.json.

entries.name: Art Objects
entries.note: the objects are named in the game's own words, keeping each table's value

entries.name: Magic Item Categories
entries.note: the game's own item kinds (weapon, armour, shield, jewellery, clothing, focus, potions, scrolls) stand for the nine categories until the named items arrive

entries.name: Awarding Magic Items
entries.note: the Magic Item Rarities table is read by the hoard's CR, since enemies scale with the land and not the party; the tracker sheet is the DM's and is not used

entries.name: Magic Items for Starting Characters
entries.note: With starting at higher levels (Expansion 14), by theme.

entries.name: Consumable Items
entries.note: Consumable items (Appendix E).

entries.name: Magic Item Special Features
entries.note: each item's maker, history and look come from the world's own past (names, places, years) instead of the d20 tables

entries.name: Appendix A: Lore Glossary
entries.note: Section 1.3: the Lore Glossary is not transplanted; Realmwalker's worlds are generated and have their own faiths.

entries.name: Appendix B: Maps
entries.note: Section 1.3: the maps are not copied; they are archetypes for new site and dungeon styles.

entries.name: Tracking Sheets
entries.note: Section 1.3: DM advice, used as design guidance, not as content. The game keeps its own records (journal, ledgers).
